index 0000000..3c40cf2
--- /dev/null
+++ b/firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/button_aa.c
@@ -0,0 +1,127 @@
+#include "ui/button_aa.h"
+
+#include <math.h>
+
+#include "gfx/legato/common/legato_color.h"
+#include "gfx/legato/core/legato_scheme.h"
+#include "gfx/legato/renderer/legato_renderer.h"
+#include "gfx/legato/widget/legato_widget.h"
+
+#define R  BUTTON_AA_RADIUS
+
+/* One shared vtable copy + the captured original paint: every button shares the
+ * same classic-skin vtable, so a single overridden copy serves all callers. */
+static leButtonWidgetVTable s_aa_vt;
+static void (*s_orig_paint)(leButtonWidget*);
+static leBool s_vt_ready = LE_FALSE;
+
+/* Corner coverage [0..255]: 255 inside the arc, 0 outside, fractional on the
+ * 1px transition band. Quadrant for the upper-left corner; other corners mirror
+ * by index. Arc centre is the inner corner of the R x R box at (R, R). */
+static uint8_t s_mask[R][R];
+static leBool s_mask_ready = LE_FALSE;
+
+static void build_mask(void)
+{
+    unsigned int x, y;
+
+    for (y = 0u; y < R; y++)
+    {
+        for (x = 0u; x < R; x++)
+        {
+            float dx  = (float)R - (float)x - 0.5f;
+            float dy  = (float)R - (float)y - 0.5f;
+            float d   = sqrtf(dx * dx + dy * dy);
+            float cov = (float)R + 0.5f - d;
+
+            if (cov < 0.0f) cov = 0.0f;
+            if (cov > 1.0f) cov = 1.0f;
+
+            s_mask[y][x] = (uint8_t)(cov * 255.0f + 0.5f);
+        }
+    }
+
+    s_mask_ready = LE_TRUE;
+}
+
+/* Smooth one corner box. (ox, oy) is its top-left in screen space; (mx, my) map
+ * a box pixel to its mask cell. bg is sampled from the box's outermost pixel,
+ * which the rounded fill leaves untouched. Only transition pixels are written. */
+static void blend_corner(int32_t ox, int32_t oy,
+                         leColor fill, leColorMode mode,
+                         leBool flip_x, leBool flip_y)
+{
+    leColor bg = leRenderer_GetPixel(flip_x ? ox + (int32_t)R - 1 : ox,
+                                     flip_y ? oy + (int32_t)R - 1 : oy);
+    unsigned int px, py;
+
+    for (py = 0u; py < R; py++)
+    {
+        for (px = 0u; px < R; px++)
+        {
+            unsigned int mx = flip_x ? (R - 1u - px) : px;
+            unsigned int my = flip_y ? (R - 1u - py) : py;
+            uint8_t cov = s_mask[my][mx];
+
+            if (cov != 0u && cov != 255u)
+            {
+                leColor c = leColorLerp(bg, fill, (uint32_t)cov * 100u / 255u, mode);
+                leRenderer_PutPixel(ox + (int32_t)px, oy + (int32_t)py, c);
+            }
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+static void aa_corners(leButtonWidget* btn)
+{
+    leRect rect;
+    leColor fill;
+    leColorMode mode;
+    int32_t rx, ry, rw, rh;
+
+    btn->fn->rectToScreen(btn, &rect);
+
+    rx = rect.x;
+    ry = rect.y;
+    rw = rect.width;
+    rh = rect.height;
+
+    /* Match the skin: pressed fills with BACKGROUND, released with BASE. */
+    fill = leScheme_GetRenderColor(btn->widget.scheme,
+                                   (btn->state != LE_BUTTON_STATE_UP)
+                                       ? LE_SCHM_BACKGROUND : LE_SCHM_BASE);
+    mode = leRenderer_CurrentColorMode();
+
+    blend_corner(rx,                  ry,                  fill, mode, LE_FALSE, LE_FALSE);
+    blend_corner(rx + rw - (int32_t)R, ry,                 fill, mode, LE_TRUE,  LE_FALSE);
+    blend_corner(rx,                  ry + rh - (int32_t)R, fill, mode, LE_FALSE, LE_TRUE);
+    blend_corner(rx + rw - (int32_t)R, ry + rh - (int32_t)R, fill, mode, LE_TRUE,  LE_TRUE);
+}
+
+static void aa_paint(leButtonWidget* btn)
+{
+    s_orig_paint(btn);
+
+    if (btn->widget.status.drawState == LE_WIDGET_DRAW_STATE_DONE &&
+        btn->widget.style.cornerRadius == R)
+    {
+        aa_corners(btn);
+    }
+}
+
+void ButtonAA_Enable(leButtonWidget* btn)
+{
+    if (!s_mask_ready)
+        build_mask();
+
+    if (!s_vt_ready)
+    {
+        s_aa_vt = *btn->fn;
+        s_orig_paint = btn->fn->_paint;
+        s_aa_vt._paint = aa_paint;
+        s_vt_ready = LE_TRUE;
+    }
+
+    btn->fn = &s_aa_vt;
+    btn->widget.fn = (const leWidgetVTable*)&s_aa_vt;
+}
diff --git a/firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/button_aa.h b/firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/button_aa.h

+#ifndef UI_BUTTON_AA_H
+#define UI_BUTTON_AA_H

+#include "gfx/legato/widget/button/legato_widget_button.h"

+#ifdef __cplusplus

+
+/* The single corner radius the AA path supports (one precomputed mask). Buttons
+ * must use this radius for the smoothing to apply. */
+#define BUTTON_AA_RADIUS  12u
+
+/* Anti-aliased rounded corners for a button. The classic skin draws rounded
+ * corners with hard, stepped edges; calling this re-points the button's vtable
+ * at a copy whose paint smooths the corner band after the normal draw. Only
+ * affects buttons with cornerRadius == BUTTON_AA_RADIUS; set the radius first.
+ * Safe to call once per button after it is constructed. */
+void ButtonAA_Enable(leButtonWidget* btn);
+
+#ifdef __cplusplus
+}

+#endif /* UI_BUTTON_AA_H */

Here's the verdict: **you got it almost exactly right — the real code on `main` is `gui`'s code — but the conflict resolution left two orphaned duplicate files behind.**

## What happened

You had the same change committed twice from a common ancestor (`069b196`):

- On **`main`**: commit `295faba` "anti-aliased rounded button corners" — added `ui/button_aa.c` + `.h`
- On **`gui`**: commit `de264e3` (same change), but then `gui` went on to commit `183ec4e` *"reorganize ui/ into screens/ + widgets/"*, which **renamed** that file to `ui/widgets/button_aa/widget_button_aa.c` + `.h`

When you merged `gui` into `main` (`3b5a887`), git saw main's `ui/button_aa.c` (live) and gui's rename — and the resolution **kept both**: main's old-path copy *and* gui's reorganized copy.

## Current state of `main`

`git diff gui main` shows the trees are identical **except** main has two extra files:

```
firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/button_aa.c   ← stale orphan (old path, from 295faba)
firmware/marvin/default/src/ui/button_aa.h   ← stale orphan
```

A new boot loader task (`ui/loader.c`) mounts the card, reads `/<card>/ui/splash.jpg` into a static buffer, builds a runtime `leImage` (format JPEG) + sets it on the widget, then `UiManager_EnableBacklight()` (backlight control moved out of `video` into `ui_manager` — the UI owns the display; it was only in `video` for historical reasons), and reveals the dashboard + brings video up. **Per-screen pre-rendered persistent canvases** (revised within-session — see bring-up #1/#2): every screen is MGS-**persistent** (built once, never torn down) and owns its own canvas/Legato-layer/HW-layer — Dashboard 0/0/BASE (RGB565), Nav 1/1/OVR1 (RGB565), Splash 2/2/OVR2 (RGBA8888, full-screen, topmost). The splash is drawn over the dashboard on OVR2; the heavy Dashboard paints **behind** it and is revealed (hide OVR2) already complete. **Off-screen paint:** all screens are built pre-scheduler (no concurrency); the normal Legato render task paints them once the scheduler is up, and the loader simply pends on the public `leRenderer_IsIdle()` before lighting the panel (no scheduler hacking — see bring-up #4/#5 for the suspend/pump dead-end). RGB888 splash via the canvas's own 32bpp mode (the canvas framework sets the HW-layer color mode from `pixelBuffer.mode`); the RGB565↔8888 BASE-swap of the first cut is gone. Missing/oversized/no-card → the panel's solid fill is the fallback. Seed `data/ui/splash.jpg` (placeholder). Design in [`ui_compositor.md`](ui_compositor.md) §12–§13. | "Turn on the display" = enable the backlight (XLCDC scans continuously from `SYS_Initialize`), so gating the backlight on splash-ready is the whole mechanism. First on-hardware run showed reveal-before-paint noise (screens shown mid-paint over uninitialized DRAM); the fix is to paint each screen to completion off-screen, then reveal — the §1 compositor ideal, enabled by persistent screens + pumping the renderer to idle off-screen. JPEG over BMP/RAW: BMP isn't Legato-decodable (only RAW/JPEG/PNG), so it would mean a custom parser + bypassing the `leImageWidget` path and would prove nothing reusable; JPEG reuses Legato's enabled decoder and **is** the album-art pre-load path. Loader is a task (not `APP_Initialize`) because SD mount + FatFs + decode block on I/O and need the scheduler. 38	| 2026-06-25 | **Re-enabled GFX Canvas Move FX to animate the nav drawer slide (reverses the earlier "FX off, do our own" call).** The nav drawer now slides in/out by animating its OVR1 canvas window position via `gfxcStartEffectMove` (DEC ease-out), rather than snapping. Fix: slide to the furthest 4-aligned X with \|X\| < NAV_W (`NAV_CLOSED_X`, derived from NAV_W — not a magic number) so the final shown frame is an in-bounds edge sliver, then `nav_fx_done` disables the layer to clear it. | Canvas Move FX over a hand-rolled stepper because the machinery already exists (just was disabled) and it's purpose-built for sliding a layer window with easing; the earlier FX-off decision was speculative (pre-slide). The only thing enforcing one-screen-at-a-time was `le_gen_init.c`'s state machine (`legato_showScreen` tears down the outgoing tree). Turning it off (and working around the MGS dangling-`le_gen_init.h` bug with a `compat/` stub) means we attach multiple panels' roots to different layers and they're all live + interactive at once. **Model:** each panel is authored as its own MGS Screen used as a *widget-tree factory* (`screenInit_` builds, `screenShow_` attaches + raises its `OnShow` composition root); `leAddRootWidget`/`leRemoveRootWidget` re-host a root onto whatever layer we choose. Layers: dashboard=BASE/0, nav=OVR1/1 (resident → "same nav over every view" free), modal song/mode dialog=OVR2/2 (sized to the dialog so live dashboard telemetry shows around it); camera=HEO outside Legato. Two verbs — **coexist** (overlay-as-layer, background live) and **replace** (swap base view on layer 0) — chosen per interaction, both owned by `ui_manager`, so the choice is reversible. `compositor.c` is promoted to `ui_manager`; per-screen/overlay modules own only their widgets+wiring. **This supersedes the earlier "parked surfaces aren't pickable / reveal-then-promote" idea in the doc** — that was a symptom of the state machine, now removed. | Greg's call to author nav + dialogs as separate MGS Screens (cleaner than overlapping layers in one Screen) collided with Legato's one-active-screen model; the resolution was to drop that model entirely rather than fight it, which the global-layerList facts make safe. Disabling the state machine also removes MGS's per-screen switch baggage outright (deleted code, not dormant) and hands us `screenInit/Show` directly. Live-coexistence (vs. freeze) was required because some dashboard telemetry must keep updating under the nav/dialog (the camera already self-updates on HEO). Per-screen modules + a `ui_manager` orchestrator keep each panel's wiring local (composition-root-per-screen) while one top-level module owns the scarce layer budget — matching the MCC-isolation idiom (own files via `user.cmake`). 3 UI layers + camera is the hard ceiling. | 
40	| 2026-06-25 | **The GFX Canvas regen pushed FreeRTOS `heap_1` past 40 KB → silent boot hang (zero DBGU output); raised `configTOTAL_HEAP_SIZE` 40960 → 100000.** Symptom: after the canvas MCC commit (`ed54f37`), marvin produced no DBGU output at all — bisected to that commit (`8de7c64` working). Not the compositor (it was stashed), and not the XLCDC OVR setup (BASE/HEO use the identical `LCDC_ATTRE`/`WAIT_ATTRS_EQ(SIP)` pre-`Start` pattern that already works, so OVR is symmetric). Root cause: the canvas additions (the dynamic `GFX_CANVAS_Task` + extra OSAL/driver allocations on the 4-layer/canvas display path) tipped cumulative `pvPortMalloc` during `SYS_Initialize` past the 40 KB `heap_1`. Because `configUSE_MALLOC_FAILED_HOOK=1` and `vApplicationMallocFailedHook()` is the MCC default (`taskDISABLE_INTERRUPTS(); for(;;){}`), the failed alloc spun with IRQs off **before** `APP_Initialize`/`log_init` (initialization.c:499) ran → no banner, indistinguishable from a dead board. **Two durable follow-ups (both carried):** (1) the heap size is **not** in `FreeRTOS.yml` — it's a raw literal in the generated `FreeRTOSConfig.h`, so the bump is an **MCC re-apply patch** (joins patch #8, also a `FreeRTOSConfig.h` edit) and will silently revert on the next regen → hang returns; set it in the MCC FreeRTOS component if it exposes Total Heap Size, else keep it on the re-apply list. (2) Patch `vApplicationMallocFailedHook` **and** `vApplicationStackOverflowHook` to emit a marker before the spin — a one-line DBGU write would have turned this multi-step bisect into an instant diagnosis. | Same silent-spin footgun already flagged for `vApplicationStackOverflowHook` (Open questions), now confirmed to bite via the malloc path too — heap exhaustion and stack overflow both present as identical dead-board hangs with the stock hooks. `heap_1` (never frees) is correct for marvin's static-allocation discipline, but MCC tasks + Legato OSAL still need it, so its size is load-bearing and must be tracked. 100000 is generous (+60 KB) headroom for now; right-size later once boot logs `xPortGetFreeHeapSize()`. Found by Greg's heap hypothesis after the XLCDC poll-loop theory was ruled out by BASE/HEO symmetry. |
